additions.name: Gießen Katzenfeld — planned data centre in the Sondergebiet Rechenzentrum

status.summary: The Universitätsstadt Gießen's official notice, signed on 2 October 2026 and listed on 5 October 2026, states that the city council adopted Bebauungsplan GI 05/23 "Katzenfeld" as a by-law on 27 August 2026 and that the plan enters into force with the notice. The in-force plan designates a 5.94 ha Sonstiges Sondergebiet "Rechenzentrum" for a data centre of about 65 MW total power intake prepared with the developer Revikon; no operator has been selected. Announced status only: a Bebauungsplan is a land-use by-law, not a building permit, and no building permit, Federal Immission Control Act permit or physical work is established.

locator.precision: Area centroid of the 5.93 ha Sonstiges Sondergebiet "Rechenzentrum" drawn in the in-force plan sheet (scale 1:1000), registered to the official basemap.de raster. It locates the zone designated for the data centre, not a building footprint, the generator yard, a parcel or a works extent; zone pixels lie up to 182 m from the point.
locator.identity_review: The plan's legend item 1.4.2 identifies the orange zone as "Sonstige Sondergebiete hier: Rechenzentrum", and Textliche Festsetzung 1.2.1 restricts it to a data centre with ancillary facilities; the measured zone area (59,274 m2) matches the Begründung's 5.94 ha Sondergebiet. The plan sheet was placed at its stated 1:1000 scale and north-up orientation by two control features shared with basemap.de, the round building at house number 29 (circle fits) and the existing combined heat and power building (footprint centroids), with residuals of 0.2 m; the Telekom building at Krofdorfer Straße 200 coincides in an overlay, and the control-point separation agrees to 0.01 m. The point lies inside the zone; the plan and Begründung name the adjacent Gießen-Nord substation as the plan area's northern neighbour.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The plan sheet is a raster scan without a coordinate grid; registration residuals of about 0.2 m at two control features do not establish the drawing or basemap accuracy, and the data-centre building position within the roughly 270 by 350 m zone is not fixed.

status.summary: The Bezirksamt Hamburg-Mitte (Fachamt Bauprüfung) granted building permit M-BP-2262-2025 on 20 July 2026 under section 72 HBauO for the new build of two data centres with generator platforms and eight car parking spaces in Gemarkung Hamm Marsch, on site plan DE-IPHH4-BA-E0-INV-LA-M-52000; the Transparenzportal Hamburg published it on 29 July 2026, the observation date used here. The permit is in force: it lapses only if execution does not begin within three years, and no suspension, withdrawal or appeal was found. A suspensive condition allows the corresponding construction works to begin only after a supplementary decision on structural stability, and tree felling needs prior species-protection clearance; neither is reported as fulfilled, so no construction stage is asserted.
status.permit_reference: Bezirksamt Hamburg-Mitte, Fachamt Bauprüfung, Baugenehmigung GZ M-BP-2262-2025 (section 72 HBauO), dated 20 July 2026, published on the Transparenzportal Hamburg on 29 July 2026
status.permit_identity_review: The permit authorises the two data-centre buildings themselves (not ancillary infrastructure). Its site plan number DE-IPHH4-BA-E0-INV-LA-M-52000 and its cited preliminary decision M-BP-864-2024 (Flurstück 949, Gemarkung Hamm Marsch, drawings numbered DE-IPHH4) tie it to Portus's IPHH4. The permit gives the preliminary decision's date as 23.05.2026, while the preliminary decision itself is dated 23 May 2025 and was published on 27 March 2026; the file number matches and the 2026 date is treated as a clerical error. The permit's own address and parcel fields are redacted; the parcel identity rests on the preliminary decision it cites.

locator.precision: Centroid of cadastral parcel Hamm Marsch 949 (Wendenstraße 285, 2,207 m2, about 49 by 68 m), the IPHH4 plot named in the preliminary decision that the building permit cites. It locates the IPHH4 project plot, not either building footprint or a works extent, and not the operator's existing IPHH2 or IPHH3 facilities or its Wendenstraße 408 office address (about 0.56 km to the east-south-east), which the selected sources do not tie to this parcel.
locator.identity_review: Preliminary decision M-BP-864-2024 names Flurstück 949 in Gemarkung Hamm Marsch for the two data centres, attaches the cadastral extract and DE-IPHH4 drawings and records the consent of the western neighbour, Flurstück 948; the building permit M-BP-2262-2025 cites that preliminary decision, uses a DE-IPHH4 site plan and permits felling trees on the Mittelkanal embankment. The council's online planning record linked from the release was not opened: the 22 October uk_ie lane reported that the Dumfries and Galloway planning portal serves a Cloudflare challenge, so no council red line was compared. The former power-station and nuclear-licensed area to the south is a different plot and is not used. Controls, residuals, traced vertices and the imagery tile digest are in the geometry facts file; no geocoder or map viewport is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The plan has no scale or coordinates; residuals measure only the fit of the consultation graphic to imagery of unknown date and accuracy, and hand tracing adds unquantified error. The 55 ha site extends about 1.3 km across, and building positions are not shown.

locator.identity_review: The form names the site 'Former Invista Site', Land at Wilton International, Redcar TS6 8JH, for the same data-centre campus described in the register record and in the applicants' amended Planning Statement (1 September 2026), which calls the project the Sembcorp Wilton International Data Centre, a joint venture of Digital Reef GB001 Limited and Sembcorp Utilities UK Limited, and centres the site on NZ 562 209, 114 m north-east of the form point. The location plan (WDC-RO-ZZ-00-D1-A-1003 rev 2) shows the red line west of the Wilton plant grid, with Kettle Beck to the west and Greystone substation to the south. Esri World Imagery viewed locally (not redistributed) shows the point on cleared former industrial land with grass, scrub and remnant hard-standing, as the Planning Statement describes. The TS6 8JH postcode centroid, 420 m north, is not used. No geocoder, estate centroid or map viewport is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The form publishes no positional accuracy; the 15.45 ha site extends a few hundred metres around the point, and the buildings' positions are shown only on plans without coordinates.
